scenes.line2: Why do we lint and format?
scenes.say: Ever wonder why interviewers care about code style? Let's see why linting and formatting matter.

scenes.label: ruff
scenes.sub: Catches errors and enforces code rules fast.
scenes.say: First up, ruff. It's a lightning-fast tool that checks your code for errors and enforces style rules.

scenes.label: black
scenes.sub: Auto-formats code to a consistent style.
scenes.say: Then there's black. It automatically formats your code so everything looks consistent, no matter who wrote it.

scenes.title: Run linting and formatting
scenes.say: Just run ruff to check for issues, and black to reformat your code. It's that simple.
I always add these tools to my continuous integration pipeline. It saves time, keeps the codebase clean, and catches problems early.

scenes.question: Is black a linting tool?
scenes.right: No, black formats code. Ruff handles linting.
scenes.say: Don't mix them up! Black formats your code, but ruff is the one that actually checks for errors and style issues.
